key_insight: This study audits the mental health interventions 41 language models recommend when the same clinical case is presented by a clinician, caregiver, or patient. The supplied abstract describes the audit's scale and design but does not report its findings.
problem_solved: Mental health advice from language models needs systematic evaluation, including whether recommendations change depending on who asks—even when the clinical information stays the same.
method: Presented 19 clinical case vignettes through three perspectives: clinician, caregiver, and patient.
Collected 35,055 free-text responses from 41 language models across five questions and extracted named interventions using a validated judge.
Had 29 models rate the full list of intervention options.
impact: The audit offers a framework for checking whether mental health recommendations depend on user perspective. AI/ML practitioners can use this approach to evaluate consistency and identify recommendations requiring clinical review.
visual_elements: Three-lane diagram: identical clinical information enters through clinician, caregiver, and patient perspectives.
Scale snapshot highlighting 41 models, 19 vignettes, five questions, and 35,055 responses.
Pipeline graphic: case prompts → model responses → intervention extraction → option ratings.
Comparison-matrix template showing intervention recommendations by user perspective, populated only when results are available.
paper_title: Curbside Chatbots: Auditing the Mental Health Interventions Large Language Models Recommend to Clinicians, Caregivers, and Patients
paper_authors: Matthew Flathers, Jill Noorily, Phuong Anh Nguyen, Mark Kalinich, Mina Fallah
